title: If you act, why fear?
odia:
କରୁ ଯଦି ଡ଼ରୁ କାହିଁକି
ଡରୁ ଯଦି କରୁ କାହିଁକି ?
literal_meaning: If you do it, why are you afraid? If you are afraid, why do you do it?
meaning_odia: କୌଣସି କାମ କରିବାକୁ ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି ନେଇ ପୁଣି ଡରରେ ଦୋଦୁଲ୍ୟମାନ ହେବାକୁ ଏହି କଥା ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ। କରିବାକୁ ଯାଉଛ ଯଦି ଡରୁଛ କାହିଁକି, ଆଉ ଡରୁଛ ଯଦି ସେ କାମରେ ପଶୁଛ କାହିଁକି—ଦୁଇ ପଟରୁ ସେହି ଦ୍ୱିଧାକୁ ଧରିଛି।
explanation: The two questions challenge the tension between choosing an action and shrinking from it. Reversing do and fear makes the listener confront that hesitation from both directions. This editorial reading takes it as a pointed challenge to indecision.
usage_example: Someone volunteers to present a rehearsed poem, then repeatedly backs away from taking the stage. A friend might use these questions to challenge the hesitation. This illustration is newly composed.
cultural_context: The second line turns the first around: doing comes before fearing, then fearing before doing. The repeated କାହିଁକି gives both halves the same questioning pressure and makes the saying easy to remember.

witnesses.note: Matches lexical wording, including first ଡ଼ରୁ and second ଡରୁ. Upload supplies two-line arrangement. Shared lineage possible.
Related form uses ଯେବେ twice instead of ଯଦି, and ଡରୁ in both positions; no explanatory gloss. Not an exact full-wording witness.

origin_note: The upload and two public lists attest closely related formulations. Their lineage, earliest use and original speaker are not established.

odia_summary: କାମ କରିବା ଓ ସେହି କାମକୁ ଡରିବାର ଦ୍ୱିଧାକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରିବା।
english_summary: Two reversed questions challenge hesitation between acting and fearing.
